council.label: Council penalty charge (PCN)
council.plain: This is a council penalty under the Traffic Management Act 2004. It is a civil penalty, not a criminal fine, and there is a free, independent tribunal if the council says no.
council.nextStep: If the council rejects your challenge it usually re-offers the discount for 14 days. If you don't pay, it sends a Notice to Owner; you then have 28 days to make formal representations, and after that 28 days to appeal to the Traffic Penalty Tribunal.

tfl.label: London penalty charge (TfL or a London borough)
tfl.plain: This is a London penalty charge. It is a civil penalty, not a criminal fine. If your challenge is rejected you can appeal for free to London Tribunals.
tfl.nextStep: If your challenge is rejected and you don't pay, a Notice to Owner follows; you then have 28 days to make formal representations, and after that 28 days to appeal to London Tribunals.

private.label: Private parking charge
private.plain: This is a private company's invoice for breaking the terms on its signs, not a fine. It can only be enforced through the civil courts. Appeal to the company first; if it says no, you can go to an independent appeals service (POPLA or the IAS) for free.
private.nextStep: If the company rejects your appeal it must give you a code for the independent appeals service: POPLA (British Parking Association members, 28 days) or the IAS (International Parking Community members, 21 days).

police.label: Police fixed penalty notice
police.plain: This is a police fixed penalty. There is no informal appeal: you either pay within 28 days or ask for a court hearing. Get free advice before choosing court.
police.challengeLabel: Pay or request a court hearing
police.nextStep: If you do nothing within 28 days the penalty can be increased by 50% and registered against you.

grounds.title: I didn't break the rule on the ticket
grounds.detail: For example, I was parked legally, or in a bay I was allowed to use.
grounds.text: The alleged contravention did not occur. {{details}}

grounds.title: The signs or lines were missing, faded or unclear
grounds.detail: Take photos of the signs and lines from where you parked.
grounds.text: The signs and/or road markings at this location were not adequate to inform a driver of the restriction. {{details}} Photographs are enclosed.

grounds.title: I was loading or unloading
grounds.detail: Heavy or bulky goods, or a delivery that took time.
grounds.text: The vehicle was being loaded or unloaded at the time, which is an exemption to this restriction. {{details}}

grounds.title: I had a valid permit, Blue Badge or ticket
grounds.detail: It was displayed, or it fell off, or the machine didn't print.
grounds.text: A valid permit, Blue Badge or pay-and-display ticket covered this vehicle at the time. {{details}} A copy is enclosed.

grounds.title: I paid for parking
grounds.detail: Pay-by-phone, app or machine. Attach the receipt or screenshot.
grounds.text: I paid for parking for this period. {{details}} Proof of payment is enclosed.

grounds.title: I was only a few minutes over
grounds.detail: Councils must allow at least 10 minutes' grace; private operators' codes also set a grace period.
grounds.text: The vehicle was within the grace period that must be allowed at the end of a paid or permitted parking period. {{details}}

grounds.title: My car broke down
grounds.text: The vehicle had broken down and could not be moved. {{details}} Evidence is enclosed.

grounds.title: There was a medical or other emergency
grounds.detail: Explain briefly; a letter from a doctor or hospital helps.
grounds.text: I ask you to cancel this charge because of an emergency: {{details}}

grounds.title: I wasn't the owner at the time
grounds.detail: I'd sold it, or not yet bought it.
grounds.text: I was not the owner of the vehicle at the time of the alleged contravention. {{details}}

grounds.title: The vehicle was stolen
grounds.text: The vehicle had been taken without my consent. {{details}}

grounds.title: I'm the keeper and I won't name the driver
grounds.detail: You don't have to say who was driving. The company can only pursue the keeper if it followed the Protection of Freedoms Act 2012 exactly.
grounds.text: I am the registered keeper. I am not obliged to name the driver and I decline to do so. Unless you can show you have met every requirement of Schedule 4 of the Protection of Freedoms Act 2012, you cannot hold me liable as keeper. {{details}}

grounds.title: The letter arrived too late
grounds.detail: A camera (ANPR) notice must reach the keeper within 14 days of the parking event.
grounds.text: The Notice to Keeper was not given within the period required by Schedule 4 of the Protection of Freedoms Act 2012. {{details}}

grounds.title: The ticket itself has mistakes
grounds.detail: Wrong registration, wrong street, wrong date, missing information.
grounds.text: The penalty charge notice contains errors and does not comply with the regulations: {{details}}

grounds.title: Something else
grounds.detail: Describe it in your own words.
